interconnectors.name: Eastern Green Link 1 (Torness to Hawthorn Pit)

ai_summary:
Scotland’s power system is currently operating in a deep decarbonization regime, anchored by a robust 4.4 GW of wind generation that is suppressing Scottish carbon intensity to a low 32 gCO2/kWh. This low-emission baseline reinforces the region’s pivotal role as the primary engine of Great Britain’s clean energy supply. However, this substantial volume of renewable yield continues to test the physical limits of cross-border transmission infrastructure.

Current telemetry records 221.1 MWh of wasted energy, pointing to active curtailment driven by export constraints along the Anglo-Scottish boundary. While curtailment remains an essential operational lever to maintain system stability and prevent thermal overloading on key corridors, it underscores stranded commercial value and missed opportunities to displace residual fossil generation elsewhere on the wider network.

To resolve these recurring export bottlenecks, strategic focus must remain on expanding transmission boundary limits, accelerating battery energy storage deployment, and scaling localized flexible demand. Over the immediate dispatch window, operational teams should closely monitor boundary transfer margins; maintaining 4.4 GW of output without escalating curtailment volumes relies heavily on maximizing interconnector headroom and leveraging dynamic storage to absorb regional surplus.
